summary: Three more articles in myseliasan's built-in manual, in all four shipped languages (12 files), taking it to 21 articles per language. Troubleshooting collects the failure modes documented across the rest of the manual into one page ordered by what actually happens rather than what is most interesting -- discovery finding nothing (almost always the fleet key), a node showing offline (check the certificate first, because auto-renew left off lets it lapse with nothing breaking loudly), a node that keeps connecting but is not in the list, a fleet rule that never fires (the text not matching beats every other cause), too many alerts, a colleague who cannot see a page, a map with no streets, blank names in a PDF, an assistant that will not answer, a setting that did not take effect, and an event with no clip -- each pointing at the article that covers it. Frequently asked questions answers what people ask before trusting a control plane with a site: whether anything leaves the network (only a map-region or model download, both optional and both with offline alternatives), whether it runs fully air-gapped, what happens to the recorders when the control plane goes down (they keep recording and detecting -- pairing adds central management and moves nothing), where video is actually stored, whether a language model is required, whether the assistant can act, why menus differ between colleagues, why a new sign-in sees nothing, why a camera gets one pin, whether two control planes can manage one node, and why a normal badge entry produced an intrusion alert. Glossary defines the 28 terms the product uses -- absence, adoption, basemap, claim code, control channel, cooldown, digest, finding, fleet key, grace delay, node access, pending, permission matrix, placement, release, self-drop, sidecar, unrecognized node, window, wipe and the rest -- each linked to the article that explains it properly. The manual now cross-links 16 of its own articles across 115 stable anchors, and four more of these questions are golden retrieval tests (32 in total).
compatibility: Backward compatible, additive only. Content only -- no code, config, schema or route changes; the articles are markdown compiled into the binary by the existing //go:embed and served by the manual endpoints that already exist. A third stable category id (reference) joins getting-started, fleet, map, agent, reports and admin. Anchors are identical across all four languages and every cross-link resolves, so the manual conformance suite (metadata, language parity, links, anchors) and the contextual-help drift guard both still pass. Binary grows by roughly 60 KB of markdown.
